note: Register of tabnas runtime dependencies that differ between this repository's ports (tabnas/admin ADR-24). tools/port-deps.cjs fails on a difference that is not listed here, and on an entry that no longer matches the manifests, so the list cannot outlive what it records. Every entry states the ports that have the dependency today, the reason, and the repair.

abnf.reason: Rust: rs/Cargo.toml declares `tabnas-abnf` with `optional = true`, turned on only by the `dialects` feature (`default = []`, so off unless asked for), and rs/src/loaders.rs uses it only under `#[cfg(feature = "dialects")]`: `compile_grammar_text` calls `tabnas_abnf::abnf_convert` for a `.abnf` file and takes `AbnfConvertOptions` and `to_pure_spec` from the same crate for all three dialects, and `dialect_versions` reads `tabnas_abnf::VERSION`; without the feature `compile_grammar_text` refuses the file as "not compiled in". TypeScript: ts/package.json declares '@tabnas/abnf' in no table, devDependencies included, yet ts/src/loaders.js names it in the `DIALECTS` table (`.abnf`) and `compileGrammarText` loads it by that name at run time through the loader's `req` function (Node's `require` unless the host passes its own), for the server and, in ts/src/generate.js, when `tabnas-lsp-gen --grammar` compiles the grammar into a generated Go or Rust server (`embeddedSpec`); a generated Node server gets the package in its own package.json dependencies instead (`emitNodeServer`). It works only where the package is installed where that `require` resolves it, and otherwise fails with "grammar dialect package not installed". Go: no non-test .go file under go/ imports a tabnas module other than github.com/tabnas/parser/go; nothing there mentions a dialect, so the Go port cannot compile grammar text and serves only what the host builds (`Config.MakeInstance` in go/server.go) or a serialized spec (`EntryFromSpecJSON` in go/lsp.go).
abnf.repair: The ports agree only when all three declare it or none does. Either ts/package.json declares '@tabnas/abnf' as an optional peer, which is what ts/src/loaders.js already loads, and the Go port gains the grammar-text lane with an import of github.com/tabnas/abnf/go in its non-test code; Go modules have no optional requirement, so go/go.mod would require it outright. Or rs/Cargo.toml drops `tabnas-abnf` from the library crate, which means the `dialects` code in rs/src/loaders.rs (`compile_grammar_text`, which `Loader::make_instance` reaches through `compile_within`) moves to a crate of its own that a host links in, or is removed. The handover page (parser/doc/handover/README.md, "Decisions waiting on the maintainer", item 3) lists, not started, an admin check comparing each package.json's peers with what ts/src imports; it does not rule on a package that ts/src loads by name at run time and declares nowhere. Ruling 10 on the same page (components "should not drag along unnecessary dependencies") bears on the choice but does not decide it. Undecided: awaits the maintainer's ruling.

csv.reason: Rust: rs/Cargo.toml declares `tabnas-csv` with `optional = true`, turned on only by the `fleet` feature (`default = []`, so off unless asked for), and rs/src uses it in one place, `fleet()` in rs/src/loaders.rs under `#[cfg(feature = "fleet")]`, which links `tabnas_csv::make` as '@tabnas/csv' so that the `tabnas-lsp` binary (`loader` in rs/src/bin/tabnas-lsp.rs) can serve the bundled registry's `csv` entry; the library needs it for nothing else. TypeScript: ts/package.json declares '@tabnas/csv' in no table, devDependencies included, and no `require` in ts/src names it literally; the server loads it at run time by the entry name in ts/data/registry.json (`pluginCandidates` in ts/src/loaders.js, through the loader's `req` function (Node's `require` unless the host passes its own), after the entry's `base`, '@tabnas/jsonic'), so it serves csv only where the package is installed where that `require` resolves it; a Node server generated by `tabnas-lsp-gen --entry csv` has the package written into its own package.json dependencies (`emitNodeServer` in ts/src/generate.js). Go: no non-test .go file under go/ imports a tabnas module other than github.com/tabnas/parser/go; the comment on `Entry` in go/lsp.go says there is no bundled registry on the Go side, and a Go server takes its grammar from the host (`Config.MakeInstance` in go/server.go) or from a serialized spec (`EntryFromSpecJSON`).
csv.repair: The ports agree only when all three declare it or none does. Either ts/package.json declares '@tabnas/csv' as an optional peer, which is what the loader already requires by name, and the Go port gains a bundled-grammar lane whose non-test code imports github.com/tabnas/csv/go, which the comment on `Entry` in go/lsp.go says the Go side does not have; Go modules have no optional requirement, so go/go.mod would require it outright. Or rs/Cargo.toml drops `tabnas-csv` from the library crate, which means `loaders::fleet`, and the build of the `tabnas-lsp` binary that calls it, move to a crate of their own, leaving the library to take parsers from its host as the Go module does. Ruling 10 on the handover page (parser/doc/handover/README.md: components "should not drag along unnecessary dependencies") bears on the choice but does not decide it. Undecided: awaits the maintainer's ruling.
